correctness.rationale: Schneider's isotropic planar identity converts the separation condition to a perimeter-excess sublevel. In a side chamber, the convex hull of the square and the exterior point replaces one side by two tangent segments, giving the stated axis-aligned ellipse; in a corner chamber the corresponding two-vertex tangent geometry gives the rotated ellipse. Their equations meet at the displayed junction, so integrating one side sector and one corner sector and multiplying by four yields the closed formula. Fresh independent evaluation reproduced that formula at \(\delta=0.01,0.1,1\), and series expansion of the exact expression gives the stated half-power asymptotic.

final_claim: For the isotropic separation body of the square \([-1,1]^2\), the boundary consists of the stated four side-ellipse and four rotated corner-ellipse arcs, and its area has the displayed exact all-parameter formula; as \(\delta\downarrow0\) the area excess has leading term \(2\pi^{3/2}\delta^{1/2}\) with the stated higher-order coefficients.
limitations: The formula uses the isotropic planar normalization in which the separation parameter corresponds to perimeter excess \(\pi\delta\).
